summary: Operator answered G-7 go, scoped to the client. Analysis resolved all 8 gaps and produced one finding that inverted the phase's shape: @mcp-ui/client@7.1.1 does NOT export UIResourceRenderer, the legacy single-iframe renderer the upstream docs still describe. Only AppRenderer and AppFrame ship, both require a hosted sandbox proxy, and @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps is a hard dependency rather than something deferrable. The phase must therefore ship the double-iframe MCP Apps architecture. Estimate revised UP to 3 sessions, against my own first draft of 2.

decisions.decision: G-7 go — operator; scoped to the client, not the @mcp-ui/* line as a whole
The ui:// resource rides inside the tool-call result content array (isUIResource is typed against EmbeddedResource), so resources/* is not required in the general case
UIResourceRenderer does not exist in 7.1.1; ship AppRenderer or AppFrame, both requiring a hosted sandbox proxy and ext-apps
The mock's method set is CONDITIONAL on host configuration — passing pre-fetched html keeps it at 3 methods; letting AppRenderer fetch adds resources/read. One coupled decision, not two.

G-2 — Vite dev-server middleware mock, transposing phase-7's vite-plugin-agui-mock.ts. Rejected extending template-mcp (stdio transport, poor cohesion) and scaffold-react-vite-axum.sh as precedent (build-time embed, not a dev API).
G-6 — adopt @mcp-ui/client@7.1.1 + @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps@1.7.5, both pinned exact; decline @mcp-ui/server (the schema is the contract instead)
G-5 — five explicit trust-boundary gates. The library's DEFAULT sandbox is 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms', safe only if the proxy is genuinely cross-origin.
G-8 — compliant-host reading; a client-only deliverable cannot be demonstrated
G-1 — direct:mcp-ui content type, adapter, schema, examples, citing upstream from the first commit. remoteDom out of scope.
G-3/G-4 — surface + resource store + sandbox proxy; scaffold-react-vite-mcp-ui.sh following the thrice-proven wrapper shape

gap_disposition.G-2: in scope — Vite mock, not template-mcp (D-004)
gap_disposition.G-3: in scope — AppRenderer/AppFrame + sandbox proxy (D-003, D-009)

estimate.direction: UP from my own first draft of 2; equal to the top of assess's 2-3 range
estimate.why_down: D-002 and D-004 removed the assumed cost of writing a protocol-speaking server
estimate.why_up_more: D-003 added the double-iframe MCP Apps architecture: hosted sandbox proxy, AppBridge, ext-apps as a real dependency, and a sandbox/CSP posture that must be reasoned about rather than accepted

open_questions_for_spec: DECISIVE: must the sandbox proxy be a genuine second origin? The library default pairs allow-scripts with allow-same-origin; upstream's mitigation is that the proxy is cross-origin. Serving it same-origin on another path would silently void that. Options: (a) cross-origin proxy, keep defaults; (b) same-origin, override permissions to drop allow-same-origin; (c) both. Settle by observing the rendered frame, not the docs.
AppRenderer or AppFrame? AppFrame takes pre-fetched html plus a hand-built AppBridge and may be the smaller surface for a mock-driven demo. Coupled to D-003a.
Is externalUrl worth including in v1, given it loads a third-party origin into the smoke test? rawHtml alone may be the honest v1.
Which change owns the five D-006 gates? Phase-8's lesson: a constraint gated over the wrong path is ungated.
verification_carried_forward: Browser-DOM gate is non-negotiable — phase-8 shipped a renderer that could not render any conformant spec, and only running it in a DOM caught that
Assert the RENDERED sandbox attribute and the proxy origin, not the source
Wire onFallbackRequest to fail loudly rather than hang on an unhandled JSON-RPC method

adversarial_review.highest_value_finding: Round 1 CRITICAL demanded provenance for D-002's central claim. Re-grounding it in shipped .d.ts revealed that UIResourceRenderer — the component I had recommended — does not exist in 7.1.1. One shortcut (citing docs instead of types) had produced four downstream errors: a phantom component, a wrong dependency verdict, a wrong architecture, and a low estimate.

tooling_gap_for_reflection: build-review-packet.sh includes neither decision-log.md nor a phase evidence/ directory, so an operator decision and any vendored upstream artifact are invisible to the judge. Round 3 raised a CRITICAL on exactly that. Worked around by vendoring types into evidence/ and citing them; the builder should include both by default.
runtime_note: G-7 runtime write-drop still in force; filesystem is authoritative.
